tex_content.html:
For a connected three-dimensional Ricci flow with nonnegative sectional curvature, $R(p,T)=0$ implies that the flow is flat on $[0,T]$.
Proof

↗ thm:curvature-evolution \sketch If curvature is positive at an earlier point, compare $R$ with a positive Dirichlet heat solution using $\partial _t(R-h)=\triangle (R-h)+2|\Ric |^2$; the strong maximum principle forces $R(p,T)>0$, a contradiction.

□

Corollary
[Local product splitting at a Ricci null eigenvalue]
